content.user_title: Plan a Realistic DevRel Content Calendar
content.value_statement: Developer-content plans slip when writing commitments ignore technical review and fixed deadlines. This skill builds quarterly publishing slots with named owners, reviewers, capacity estimates, and reserved reactive time.
actual_capabilities: Compare evergreen, launch-dominated, and event-led quarter shapes against team goals and constraints.
Estimate production effort across research, drafting, working code, technical review, publishing, and reply load.
Build weekly slots with surfaces, pillars, journey stages, shelf-life labels, owners, reviewers, and supporting evidence.
Schedule preparation, follow-up, repurposing, and refresh work alongside fixed release and event dates.
Audit an existing calendar against ownership, capacity, evidence, and content-mix checks.
Define monthly reviews using publish rate, mix drift, anchor coverage, and review-to-publication lead time.
limitations: Plans content slots but does not write the individual articles, guides, release notes, or talks.
Requires user-provided audience goals, dates, availability, and historical output for reliable estimates.
Provides a planning workflow, not an automated publishing service or calendar synchronization integration.
Uses proposed baselines and limited case-study benchmarks, not guaranteed throughput or traffic forecasts.

use_cases.title: Plan a release-heavy quarter
use_cases.description: Coordinate launch preparation, evergreen guides, and follow-up slots without committing all capacity to one release date.

use_cases.title: Size a small team's publishing workload
use_cases.description: Identify technical review constraints and replace expensive formats with work that fits available capacity.

use_cases.title: Audit an existing community content plan
use_cases.description: Find missing owners, unsupported topics, coverage gaps, and overloaded weeks before proposing the smallest necessary changes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a quarterly calendar
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan next quarter's developer content for [product]. Ask about our audience, goals, fixed dates, and capacity before recommending a quarter shape.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: build a plan through the guided interview.

prompt_templates.title: Check what the team can ship
prompt_templates.prompt: We have [writer availability] and [reviewer availability] for [quarter]. Assess [proposed formats and counts], estimate production passes, and recommend cuts with named slack.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test workload against writing and review constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a slipping calendar
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this existing developer-content calendar: [calendar]. Report failed checks in damage order and propose minimal changes. Ask for missing evidence, owners, reviewers, and capacity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: repair a plan without rebuilding it.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a constrained launch quarter
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [quarter] around [release dates], [accepted talks], and [agency commitments]. Use [audience goals], [capacity], and [past results]. Validate each plan section before proceeding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate multiple deadlines and production dependencies.

output_examples.input: Plan Q3 for a developer tool with a week-four release, one writer, and a technical reviewer available three hours weekly.
output: Quarter shape: confirm whether launch visibility or long-term adoption matters most before assigning dates.
Capacity model: estimate reviewer passes for each format and reserve 20% of estimated capacity for reactive work.
Release coverage: schedule preparation before week four and follow-up afterward, with named owners and reviewers.
Next input needed: team names, format estimates, audience priorities, and last quarter's shipped work.

output_examples.input: Audit thirteen weekly blog slots owned by 'content team', with no reviewers, evidence, preparation work, or open capacity.
output: Ownership check failed: assign a specific owner and reviewer to every committed slot.
Capacity check failed: reduce commitments to leave named reactive capacity.
Coverage check failed: add relevant documentation and another surface, with at least two journey stages.
Evidence check failed: attach observed demand or a written hypothesis to each topic.
Anchor check failed: schedule preparation and follow-up around each fixed deadline.

best_practices: Provide last quarter's shipped and delayed work before accepting default throughput assumptions.
Name each technical reviewer and estimate review passes before assigning publishing weeks.
Validate anchors, mix, capacity, slots, and review rules separately, with explicit decisions at each stage.
anti_patterns: Fill every week without reserving capacity for reactive work or delayed reviews.
Treat repurposed assets, agency writing, or conference preparation as work that consumes no internal capacity.
Present an evergreen ratio or one company's publishing output as a universal benchmark.

faq.question: Does this skill write the scheduled content?
faq.answer: No. It plans the quarter and assigns slots. Individual articles, guides, release notes, and talks belong to separate format-specific workflows.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the product, quarter, audience, funding goal, fixed dates, writer availability, reviewer availability, and recent publishing results.

faq.question: Can it review a calendar I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. Audit mode checks the existing plan, orders failures by impact, and recommends the smallest changes needed to clear its checks.

faq.question: Does 80/20 mean evergreen versus trending content?
faq.answer: No. Its 80/20 convention divides committed capacity from reactive room. The evergreen share depends on the chosen quarter shape and team evidence.

faq.question: Will it publish or synchronize my calendar?
faq.answer: No automated publishing or synchronization integration is included. The output is a planning document with anchors, mix ratios, capacity, slots, and review metrics.

faq.question: Does it store planning context?
faq.answer: The instructions support persistent memory when available. File-based memory uses devrel-context.md; another existing memory system may be used instead.
